clue.text: Lower volume and mark the place

definitions.meaning: to reduce the sound level on a radio or television
to fold over the corner of a page to keep your place in a book

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both reducing a dial's setting and folding a page corner as a bookmark.

clue.text: Grapple with two animals when climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: Wrestling with a pair of beasts as they scale a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' reverses the whole of ELKCAT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to grapple with it.

clue.text: He sets the stage for group travelling

definitions.text: He sets the stage for group travelling

parts.words: He sets the stage for group travelling
parts.note: a touring band's helper who sets up equipment as they move from venue to venue

explanation.surface: A stage manager readying the venue for a touring company.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie travels with a band, setting up the stage gear for each show.

clue.text: Stagecoach needs proper care

definitions.meaning: a public stagecoach, especially in France

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a French public coach and careful, persistent attention.

clue.text: Sign of cowardice that gives away the wife-hater

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are dispersed and reformed, given away in a new order

explanation.surface: A misogynist betraying his fear of women.
explanation.walkthrough: A white feather was handed to men in Britain in the First World War to brand them cowards.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing the white feather is a traditional emblem of cowardice.

clue.text: One with a degree in charge of verse form

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining an adjective that also serves as a noun for a metrical line

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a degree

explanation.surface: A graduate who is in charge of something, perhaps a poetry workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: The degree here is MB, Bachelor of Medicine, not the more obvious BA or MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic metre, built from unstressed-stressed feet, is a classic poetic form of verse.

clue.text: On which goods may go out or back

definitions.text: On which goods may go out or back

parts.words: On which goods may go out or back
parts.note: items sent to a customer on trial, which may be kept or returned

explanation.surface: Shop goods being sent out and returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal British phrase 'on appro' is short for on approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on approval may be returned if the customer is not satisfied.

clue.text: Rolls up at tea party?

parts.note: pictures bread buns being thrown in a fight, rather than people arriving

explanation.surface: Guests arriving at an afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls up' reads as arrives, but rolls are buns and 'up' suggests a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunfight is British slang for a tea party or a lively, noisy gathering.

clue.text: Rival outside left is accomplished

indicators.note: the word for rival goes around the letter for left

parts.note: to rival is to compete

explanation.surface: An opponent standing outside the left side of a pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete means finished, as an accomplished task is done.

clue.text: Comedian cut by a clergyman

indicators.note: the comedian's name is split open by the next piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin, the silent-film comedian
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic performer is interrupted by a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a school, hospital or regiment.

clue.text: 25 in English money initially for someone giving a name

indicators.note: the slang sum sits within the other two letters, one placed either side
only the opening letter of the word money is taken

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: A sum of twenty-five in English currency, as a puzzle about cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25 here is not a cross-reference but the number itself: a pony is British slang for £25.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a person after whom something, such as a place or invention, is named.

clue.text: I rode in state: it's enough to make one lose one's bearings

definitions.text: I rode in state: it's enough to make one lose one's bearings

indicators.note: the letters lose their order, as someone confused does, and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dignitary riding in a ceremonial procession feels dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, while 'lose one's bearings' also signals rearranging the letters of 'I rode in state'.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorientate someone is to confuse them so they lose their sense of direction.

clue.text: Being prone to deceit

definitions.meaning: ... flat, face down or stretched out

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stretched out horizontally and the act of telling untruths.

clue.text: Drift round college, to hear considered view on paper

indicators.note: the word for the drift is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a drift or current

indicators.note: the college name is said aloud, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: Wandering about a university, listening to a newspaper's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is an Oxford college; its sound is respelt ORIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is a newspaper article giving the paper's considered opinion.

clue.text: Confidence 'so maintained when bowler's on top?

definitions.text: Confidence 'so maintained when bowler's on top?

parts.words: Confidence 'so maintained when bowler's on top?
parts.note: a secret kept to oneself, pictured as something stowed beneath a bowler hat worn on the head

explanation.surface: A cricket match where the bowler is dominating and confidence is kept up.
explanation.walkthrough: A bowler is a hat as well as a cricketer; the idiom means kept secret, a confidence kept beneath one's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes keeping information secret, as one keeps a confidence.

clue.text: Whisk, for example, consumer round our country

indicators.note: the first two pieces together go around the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: an eater consumes food
GB, Great Britain, from a British paper's viewpoint

explanation.surface: A whisk as a typical kitchen tool, an eater around Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-beater is a kitchen whisk for beating eggs.

clue.text: Odds on racehorse right? It's a gem

parts.note: SP is the starting price, betting odds
Arkle was a famous Irish steeplechaser

explanation.surface: Betting odds on a horse being right, a real gem of a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkle won three Cheltenham Gold Cups in the 1960s; 'on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkler is slang for a diamond or other gem.

clue.text: Discontinue meeting and regroup round crank

indicators.note: to crank is to turn, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Ending a meeting so that people can regroup.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue a parliament is to discontinue its session without dissolving it.

clue.text: With racehorses, first tighten controls on spending

indicators.note: this places the word for tighten ahead of the racehorses in the answer

parts.note: to purse the lips is to tighten them
a string is a stable's group of racehorses

explanation.surface: A trainer with horses must first rein in costs.
explanation.walkthrough: A string is the set of horses kept by one trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever holds the purse strings controls how money is spent.

clue.text: Sweet child of Italian composer missing in island

indicators.note: the next letters are removed from the composer's name

parts.note: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer's sweet child goes missing on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic, sweet-faced child.

clue.text: Operatic heroine, one betrayed by sweetheart

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to sell someone out is to betray them
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: An opera heroine betrayed by the man she loves.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: He looks after flocks in the country

definitions.text: He looks after flocks in the country

parts.words: He looks after flocks in the country
parts.note: reads as a shepherd, but the flocks are congregations of a church district outside the towns

explanation.surface: A shepherd tending sheep out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England this clergyman oversees a group of parishes.
explanation.definitionFit: This Anglican cleric supervises the parish priests, or flocks, of a rural deanery.

clue.text: Fast release

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dissolute in morals and to set free.

clue.text: General disposition detectable using stethoscope

indicators.note: the answer can be found within the letters of the instrument's name

explanation.surface: A doctor gauges a patient's temperament with a medical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or disposition of a person or group.

clue.text: Many show no resistance in an ankle-fetter

indicators.note: the letter for resistance is removed from the shackle

parts.note: a leg iron is a shackle for the ankle
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A prisoner in shackles who offers no resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as an adjective means very numerous, as in 'their names are legion'.

clue.text: Got through a viva, say, to do with priestly duties

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is to be heard as a sound-alike

parts.note: passed an oral examination

explanation.surface: A student passes an oral exam on a church topic.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva is an oral examination, so passing one is 'passed oral'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral care is the spiritual guidance given by a priest to a congregation.

clue.text: Referee shortly will change into jacket

indicators.note: the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order
the word is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A referee will change into a jacket after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims REFEREE to REFERE, and 'will change' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a thick double-breasted jacket, as worn by sailors.

clue.text: Pooh qualified to be accepted

definitions.note: an infinitive phrase standing for an adjective meaning able to be tolerated

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is a bear
able means competent or qualified

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh earning his qualifications and being accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bearable can be tolerated, so it is fit to be accepted.
